title.zh: 卷二百六十 列傳第十九 曹翰 楊嗣 党進 李漢瓊 劉遇 李懷忠 米信 田重進 劉廷翰 崔翰
title.en: Volume 260 Biographies 19: Cao Han, Yang Si, Dang Jin, Li Hanqiong, Liu Yu, Li Huaizhong, Mi Xin, Tian Zhongjin, Liu Tinghan, Cui Han
title.raw: 卷二百六十 列傳第十九 曹翰 楊嗣 党進 李漢瓊 劉遇 李懷忠 米信 田重進 劉廷翰 崔翰 Volume 260 Biographies 19: Cao Han, Yang Si, Dang Jin, Li Hanqiong, Liu Yu, Li Huaizhong, Mi Xin, Tian Zhongjin, Liu Tinghan, Cui Han

sentences.zh: 曹翰，大名人。

translations.literal: Cao Han was a native of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Han came from Daming.

sentences.zh: 少為郡小吏，好使氣陵人，不為鄉里所譽。

translations.literal: In youth he served as a petty clerk in the commandery; he delighted in throwing his weight about and humiliating others, and was not praised by his home district.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he worked as a petty county clerk, prone to browbeating others, and won no esteem in his community.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，周太祖鎮鄴，與語，奇之，以隸世宗帳下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyou era, when Emperor Taizu of Zhou was stationed at Ye, he conversed with him, found him remarkable, and placed him under the heir apparent's command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyou reign, when the future Zhou Taizu was posted at Ye, he spoke with Han, took a liking to him, and assigned him to the heir apparent's staff.

sentences.zh: 世宗鎮澶淵，署為牙校，入尹開封，留翰在鎮。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent was stationed at Chanyuan, he appointed him as yaxiao; when he entered Kaifeng as metropolitan prefect, he left Han at the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent took command at Chanyuan, he made Han a staff officer; when he went to govern Kaifeng as metropolitan prefect, he left Han behind at the post.

sentences.zh: 會太祖寢疾，翰不俟召，歸見世宗，密謂曰：「主上不豫，王為冢嗣，不侍醫藥而決事於外廷，失天下望。」

translations.literal: When the emperor fell gravely ill, Han without awaiting summons returned and saw the heir apparent, telling him secretly: "The sovereign is unwell. You as heir apparent do not attend him with medicines yet decide affairs in the outer court—you will lose the empire's regard."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu grew seriously ill, Han returned unbidden to see the heir apparent and said in private, "Your father is ill. As heir you ought to be at his bedside, not conducting state business in the outer court—the realm will think less of you."

sentences.zh: 世宗悟，即入侍，以府事屬翰總決。

translations.literal: The heir apparent understood, immediately entered to attend, and entrusted prefectural affairs to Han for overall decision.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent took the point, went in at once to nurse his father, and put Han in charge of all prefectural business.

sentences.zh: 及世宗即位，補供奉官，從征高平，參豫謀畫。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent took the throne, Han was made a palace service officer; he followed the campaign at Gaoping and took part in planning.
translations.idiomatic: After the heir apparent became emperor, Han was appointed a palace attendant; he accompanied the Gaoping campaign and joined in strategic deliberations.

sentences.zh: 尋遷樞密承旨，護塞決河。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, protecting the frontier and opening river channels.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and charged with frontier defense and river-control works.

sentences.zh: 世宗征淮南，留鎧甲千數在正陽，既而得降卒八百，部送歸京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, he left several thousand suits of armor at Zhengyang; later he obtained eight hundred surrendered troops and ordered them escorted back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Shizong's Huainan campaign, several thousand suits of armor were left at Zhengyang; later eight hundred captives were ordered escorted to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時翰適從京師來詣，過正陽十數里許遇之，慮劫兵器為叛，矯殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Han happened to be coming from the capital on assignment; ten-odd li past Zhengyang he encountered them, feared they might seize weapons and rebel, and on false authority killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Han happened to be traveling from the capital just then; a dozen li or so beyond Zhengyang he met the column, feared they might seize the stored arms and rise in revolt, and had them put to death on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 及見世宗，具言其事，世宗不悅。

translations.literal: When he saw Shizong he reported the whole affair in detail; Shizong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported what he had done, Shizong was displeased.

sentences.zh: 翰曰：「賊以困歸我，非心服也，所得器甲，盡在正陽，苟為所劫，是復生一淮南矣。」

translations.literal: Han said: "The enemy surrendered to us out of distress, not from true submission; all captured armor and weapons are at Zhengyang—if they seized them, we would spawn another Huainan rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Han replied, "They came to us beaten, not reconciled in heart. All the captured arms lie at Zhengyang—if they seized them, we would be facing a second Huainan uprising."

sentences.zh: 因不之罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: On that account he went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 從征瓦橋關，會班師，留知雄州。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign at Waqiao Pass; when the army withdrew he was left as acting prefect of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the Waqiao Pass campaign; when the troops withdrew he was left in charge of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗大漸，諭范質等以王著為相，翰為宣徽使。

translations.literal: As Shizong grew critically ill, he instructed Fan Zhi and others to make Wang Zhu chancellor and Han commissioner of the Palace Service.
translations.idiomatic: As Shizong lay dying, he directed Fan Zhi and the others to appoint Wang Zhu chancellor and Han commissioner of the Palace Service.

sentences.zh: 質以著嗜酒，翰飾詐而專，並寢之。

translations.literal: Fan Zhi, because Zhu was fond of wine and Han was crafty and domineering, set both proposals aside.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhi, finding Zhu too fond of drink and Han too slippery and overbearing, shelved both appointments.

sentences.zh: 改德州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han was made prefect of Dezhou instead.

sentences.zh: 宋初，從征澤、潞，還，改濟州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he followed the campaigns in Ze and Lu; on return he was made prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he campaigned in Ze and Lu prefectures; when he returned he was transferred to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，太祖親征西蜀，移刺均州，澗谷深險，翰令鑿石通道，師旋以濟；

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, when Taizu personally campaigned against Western Shu, Han was moved to be prefect of Junzhou; ravines and valleys were deep and perilous—Han ordered a stone passage cut so that on the army's return they could cross.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 2 (964), when Taizu marched in person against Shu, Han was posted to Junzhou. Where ravines were steep and narrow he had a rock-cut road opened so the returning army could pass.

sentences.zh: 詔兼西南諸州轉運使，自石門徑趨歸州，餉運不乏，由夔、萬入會王全斌軍，成都以平。

translations.literal: He was ordered concurrently to serve as transport commissioner for the southwestern prefectures; from Shimen he struck straight for Guizhou, and supplies never ran short; through Kuizhou and Wanzhou he joined Wang Quanbin's army, and Chengdu was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He was also named transport commissioner for the southwest, struck from Shimen straight toward Guizhou, and kept the supply lines full; marching through Kuizhou and Wanzhou he linked up with Wang Quanbin's forces, and Chengdu fell.

sentences.zh: 時全師雄擁眾十萬餘據郫縣叛，謀窺成都，翰率兵會劉光毅、曹彬等討平之。

translations.literal: At that time Quan Shixiong mustered a force of more than a hundred thousand, held Pixian in rebellion, and plotted to threaten Chengdu; Han led troops to join Liu Guangyi, Cao Bin, and others in suppressing them.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Shixiong meanwhile rallied over a hundred thousand men at Pixian in revolt, eyeing Chengdu; Han led forces to join Liu Guangyi, Cao Bin, and others in crushing the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 未幾，軍校呂翰殺武懷節，據嘉州以叛，翰及諸將奪其城。

translations.literal: Before long the army officer Lü Han killed Wu Huaijie and seized Jiazhou in rebellion; Han and the other generals recaptured the city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, a company officer named Lü Han killed Wu Huaijie and seized Jiazhou; Cao Han and his colleagues took the city back.

sentences.zh: 諜知賊約三鼓復來攻，翰戒知更使緩，向晨猶二鼓，賊眾不集而潰，因而破之，劍南遂平。

translations.literal: Spies learned the rebels had arranged to attack again at the third watch; Han warned the watch-keepers to slow the drums—at dawn it was still the second watch, the rebel host failed to gather and scattered, and he broke them, so Jiannan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported the enemy meant to attack again at the third watch. Han told the timekeepers to beat the watches slowly—by daybreak they were still on the second watch, the rebels never assembled and melted away, and he routed them, bringing Jiannan under control.

sentences.zh: 師還，遷蔡州團練使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted to regimental commissioner of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was made regimental commissioner of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，從征太原，復為行營都壕砦使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he followed the Taiyuan campaign and was again made commander of encampments and fortifications for the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 2 (969) he joined the Taiyuan expedition and was again named chief of headquarters entrenchments and stockades.

sentences.zh: 既班師，會河決澶州，令翰董其役，翰出銀器助役，沉所乘白馬以祭；

translations.literal: After the withdrawal, when the Yellow River broke its banks at Chunzhou, he was ordered to oversee the works; Han contributed silver vessels to aid the labor and sank the white horse he rode as an offering;
translations.idiomatic: After the army came home, the Yellow River burst its banks at Chunzhou and Han was put in charge of the repair. He donated silverware to support the work and sacrificed his own white horse to the river;

sentences.zh: 復決陽武，再護役，皆有成績。

translations.literal: It broke again at Yangwu and he again supervised the labor, each time with success.
translations.idiomatic: When it broke again at Yangwu he oversaw the work a second time, both efforts succeeding.

sentences.zh: 將征江南，命翰率兵先赴荊南，改行營先鋒使，進克池州。

translations.literal: When the Jiangnan campaign was planned, Han was ordered to lead troops first to Jingnan, was made vanguard of the field army, and advanced to capture Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before the conquest of Jiangnan he was sent ahead into Jingnan as field-army vanguard and took Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 金陵平，江州軍校胡德、牙將宋德明據城拒命。

translations.literal: After Jinling fell, the Jiangzhou officers Hu De and ya-jiang Song Deming held the city and refused orders.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jinling had surrendered, the Jiangzhou officer Hu De and deputy Song Deming still held the city in defiance.

sentences.zh: 翰率兵攻之，凡五月而陷，屠城無噍類，殺兵八百。

translations.literal: Han led troops to attack; after five months it fell; he slaughtered the city to the last living thing and killed eight hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Han besieged it for five months, then stormed it, slaughtering every living soul in the city and executing eight hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 所略金帛以億萬計，偽言欲致廬山東林寺鐵羅漢像五百頭於京師，因調巨艦百艘，載所得以歸。

translations.literal: Plunder in gold and silk ran to hundreds of millions; he falsely claimed he wished to transport five hundred iron arhat statues from Donglin Temple on Lushan to the capital, and thus requisitioned a hundred great ships to carry his spoils home.
translations.idiomatic: He looted wealth reckoned in the hundreds of millions, pretended he meant to ship five hundred iron arhat statues from Donglin Temple on Mount Lu to the capital, and requisitioned a hundred large vessels to carry his haul away.

sentences.zh: 錄功遷桂州觀察使、判潁州。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was promoted to military commissioner of Guizhou and superintendent of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his recorded merit he was made military commissioner of Guizhou and superintendent of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，從征太原，為攻城南面都部署。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo he joined the Taiyuan campaign as overall deployer for the southern assault on the city.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4 (979) he campaigned against Taiyuan as supreme commander of the southern siege.

sentences.zh: 與崔彥進、李漢瓊、劉遇三節度分部攻城，翰攻東北，而劉遇攻西北，與劉繼元直，城尤險固，遇欲與翰易處，翰言：「觀察使班次下，當部東北。」

translations.literal: He, Cui Yanjin, Li Hanqiong, and Liu Yu—the three military commissioners—divided forces to assault the city; Han attacked the northeast while Liu Yu attacked the northwest opposite Liu Jiyuan, where the walls were especially strong; Yu wished to swap sectors with Han, and Han said: "Your rank as military commissioner is lower—you should hold the northeast."
translations.idiomatic: He, Cui Yanjin, Li Hanqiong, and Liu Yu split the siege: Han took the northeast, Liu Yu the northwest facing Liu Jiyuan's strongest walls. Yu wanted to trade sectors; Han said, "Your commission outranks mine in title but not in peril—the northeast is where you belong."

sentences.zh: 遇堅欲易之，數日不決。

translations.literal: Yu insisted on swapping; for several days it was unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu pressed the swap for days without resolution.

sentences.zh: 上慮諸將不協，遣諭翰曰：「卿智勇無雙，西北面非卿不能當也。」

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing the generals would not cooperate, sent instructions to Han: "Your wisdom and courage are without peer—the northwest sector is something only you can hold."
translations.idiomatic: Worried the generals might quarrel, the emperor sent word to Han: "No one matches your skill—the northwest is yours alone to hold."

sentences.zh: 翰乃奉詔，築土山瞰城中，數日而就，繼元甚恐。

translations.literal: Han then obeyed the edict, built an earthen mound overlooking the city, completed it in several days, and Jiyuan was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Han obeyed, threw up an earth mound overlooking the walls in a few days, and Liu Jiyuan was shaken.

sentences.zh: 軍中乏水，城西十餘里谷中有娘子廟，翰往禱之，穿渠得水，人馬以給。

translations.literal: The army lacked water; in a valley ten-odd li west of the city was Niangzi Shrine; Han went to pray, dug a channel and obtained water, supplying men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When water ran short, Han prayed at the Lady's Shrine west of the city, opened a channel, and supplied the entire force.

sentences.zh: 又從征幽州，率所部攻城東南隅，卒掘土得蟹以獻。

translations.literal: He also campaigned to Youzhou, led his troops against the southeast corner of the wall, and soldiers digging earth found crabs and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On the Youzhou campaign his men digging earth at the southeast corner found crabs and brought them to him.

sentences.zh: 翰謂諸將曰：「蟹水物而陸居，失所也。

translations.literal: Han told the generals: "Crabs are creatures of water yet dwell on land—they have lost their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Han told the other commanders, "Crabs belong in the water yet live on land—they are out of their element.

sentences.zh: 且多足，彼援將至，不可進拔之象，況蟹者解也，其班師乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover they have many legs—this is a sign that enemy reinforcements are coming and we cannot advance and capture; besides, 'crab' (xie) suggests 'yield' (xie)—shall we withdraw the army?"
translations.idiomatic: With all those legs, reinforcements are coming and we cannot take the city. And xie 'crab' puns on retreat—ought we not withdraw?"

sentences.zh: 已而果驗。

translations.literal: Before long it proved true.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 五年，從幸大名，拜威塞軍節度，仍判潁州，復命為幽州行營都部署。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he accompanied the emperor to Daming, was made military commissioner of the Weisai Army while still superintendent of Yingzhou, and was again appointed overall deployer of the Youzhou field army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he accompanied the court to Daming, was made commissioner of the Weisai army while retaining Yingzhou, and was again named supreme commander of the Youzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 詔督役開南河，自雄達莫，以通漕運，議築大堤以捍之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to supervise labor opening the Southern River from Xiong to Damo to open grain transport, with plans to build a great dike to contain it.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to open the Southern Canal from Xiongzhou to Damo for transport and to raise a great dike against floods.

sentences.zh: 翰遣徒數萬，伐巨木於漢境，遣騎五，授五色旗為斥候，前遇丘陵、水澤、寇賊、煙火，則各舉其旗以為應，又起烽燧於境上，敵疑不敢近塞，得巨木數萬以濟用，訖事歸鎮。

translations.literal: Han sent tens of thousands of laborers to fell huge trees in Han territory, dispatched five horsemen given banners of five colors as scouts; when they encountered hills, marshes, bandits, or beacon smoke, each raised the corresponding banner as signal; he also raised beacon fires on the frontier so the enemy dared not approach the border; he obtained tens of thousands of great timbers for the project, and when the work was done returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: He sent tens of thousands of men into Liao territory to fell great trees, posted five riders with colored signal banners to mark hills, wetlands, raiders, and fires, lit frontier beacons so enemies kept their distance, brought back tens of thousands of timbers for the works, then returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 翰在郡歲久，征斂苛酷，政因以弛。

translations.literal: Han had long been in the prefecture; his levies were harsh and cruel, and administration accordingly grew lax.
translations.idiomatic: After long years in command his exactions grew merciless and governance slackened.

sentences.zh: 上以其有功，每優容之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his past merit, continually indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor indulged him because of past service.

sentences.zh: 會汝陰令孫崇望詣闕，訴翰私市兵器，所為多不法。

translations.literal: When Sun Chongwang, magistrate of Ruyin, came to court and accused Han of privately trading in weapons and many unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruyin magistrate Sun Chongwang reached court and charged Han with illicit arms dealing and other crimes.

sentences.zh: 詔遣御史滕中正乘傳鞫之，獄具，當棄市，上貸其罪，削官爵，流錮登州。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered investigating censor Teng Zhongzheng to travel post-haste to try him; the case was complete and he deserved execution, but the emperor spared his life, stripped rank and titles, and exiled him under guard to Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Zhongzheng was sent to investigate; the case warranted death, but the emperor commuted the sentence, stripped his titles, and banished him to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，起為右千牛衛大將軍、分司西京。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was called back as general of the Right Palace Gate Corps and assigned to the Western Capital in nominal duty.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 2 (985) he was restored as general of the Right Palace Gate Corps with nominal duty at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，召入為左千牛衛上將軍，賜錢五百萬，白金五千兩。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as senior general of the Left Palace Gate Corps and given five million in cash and five thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4 he was recalled as senior general of the Left Palace Gate Corps and given five million cash and five thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，卒，年六十九，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he died at age sixty-nine and was posthumously made Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chunhua 3 (992) at sixty-nine and was posthumously honored as Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 上命遷其四子守謙、守能、守節、守貴官，其六子守讓、守贄、守澄、守恩、守英、守吉皆補殿直。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered four sons—Shouqian, Shouneng, Shoujie, Shougui—promoted in rank; six sons Shourang, Shouzhi, Shoucheng, Shouen, Shouying, and Shouji were all given posts as palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons were advanced in office; six others were appointed palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 翰陰狡多智數，好誇誕，貪冒貨賂，飲酒至數斗不亂。

translations.literal: Han was secretly cunning, full of stratagems, fond of boastful exaggeration, greedy for bribes, and could drink several dozen cups without disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly crafty and calculating, he loved grandiose talk, coveted bribes, and could drink several dozen cups without staggering.

sentences.zh: 每奏事上前，雖數十條，皆默識不少差。

translations.literal: Each time he memorialized before the throne, even on dozens of points he remembered them all without error.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported at court on dozens of points, he recalled every one without a slip.

sentences.zh: 嘗作《退將詩》曰：「曾因國難披金甲，恥為家貧賣寶刀。」

translations.literal: He once composed "Poem of a Retired General," saying: "Once I donned golden armor for the nation's peril; I would be shamed if poverty forced me to sell my treasured sword."
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a "Retired General" poem: "I wore golden armor in the nation's peril; I would be shamed to sell my treasured blade for poverty."

sentences.zh: 翰直禁日，因語及之。

translations.literal: On a day when Han was on palace duty he mentioned it in conversation.
translations.idiomatic: On palace duty he happened to mention the lines.

sentences.zh: 上憫其意，故有銀錢之賜。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity on his meaning, and therefore granted him silver and cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved by the hint, made the silver and cash grant.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，賜諡武毅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping he was given the posthumous name Wuyi (Steadfast Martial).
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 1 (998) he received the posthumous name Steadfast Martial.

sentences.zh: 楊信，瀛州人。

translations.literal: Yang Xin was a native of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin came from Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初名義。

translations.literal: His original name was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally named Yi.

sentences.zh: 顯德中，隸太祖麾下為裨校。

translations.literal: During Xiande he was attached to Taizu's command as a deputy officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiande era he served under Taizu as a deputy officer.

sentences.zh: 宋初，權內外馬步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he held acting office as deputy commander-in-chief of the inner and outer horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty he was acting deputy commander of the inner and outer horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，領賀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was made prefect of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2 (961) he received Hezhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 改鐵騎、控鶴都指揮使，遷殿前都虞候，領漢州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was made commander of the Iron Cavalry and Cranes regiments, promoted to deputy commander of the Palace Front, and given the defense commissioner title for Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the Iron Cavalry and Cranes regiments, rose to deputy commander of the Palace Front Corps, and held the Hanzhou defense commission.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，親郊，為儀仗都部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande, when the emperor personally performed suburban sacrifice, he was made overall deployer of ceremonial guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu performed the suburban rites in early Qiande, Xin directed the ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 四年，信病瘖，上幸其第，賜錢二百萬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Xin fell ill with loss of speech; the emperor visited his residence and gave him two million cash.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande 4 he lost his voice to illness; the emperor visited his home and gave him two million cash.

sentences.zh: 五年，改靜江軍節度。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made military commissioner of the Jingjiang army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was made military commissioner of Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，散指揮都知杜廷進等將為不軌，謀泄，夜啟玄武門，召信逮捕，遲明，十九人皆獲，上親訊而誅之。

translations.literal: In Kaibao 2, Du Tingjin of the Scattered Command and others plotted sedition; the plot leaked; at night they opened the Xuanwu Gate and summoned Xin to arrest them; by dawn all nineteen were seized; the emperor personally interrogated and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 2 (969), Du Tingjin of the Scattered Command regiment and others plotted treason; when the plot surfaced, they opened the Xuanwu Gate at night and called Xin to make arrests; by dawn all nineteen were in custody, and the emperor examined and executed them himself.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷殿前都指揮使，改領建武軍節度。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to commander of the Palace Front and made military commissioner of Jianwu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he became commander of the Palace Front and military commissioner of Jianwu.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗令御龍直習水戰於後池，有鼓噪聲，信居玄武門外，聞之，遽入，服皂綈袍以見。

translations.literal: Taizu once ordered the Imperial Dragon guard to practice naval warfare in the rear pond; there was a clamor of drums; Xin was outside the Xuanwu Gate, heard it, hurried in wearing a black silk robe to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Taizu had the Imperial Dragon guard practicing on the rear pond and a hubbub arose, Xin, stationed outside the Xuanwu Gate, rushed in wearing a plain black robe.

sentences.zh: 上謂曰：「吾教水戰爾，非有他也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I am teaching naval warfare—that is all, nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I am only drilling them in river fighting—nothing more."

sentences.zh: 出，上目送之，謂左右曰：「真忠臣也。」

translations.literal: As he left, the emperor watched him go and told attendants: "A true loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: As Xin left, the emperor watched him go and told attendants, "There is a true loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 九年，授義成軍節度。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was given the Yicheng military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he received the Yicheng military commission.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，改鎮寧軍，並領殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to Zhenning and continued as commander of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 he was moved to Zhenning while keeping command of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 三年春，以瘖疾在告，俄卒，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, on sick leave for his speech disability, he soon died and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 3, on leave for his muteness, he died soon after and was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 信雖瘖疾而質實自將，善部分士卒，指顧申儆，動有紀律，故見信任，而終始無疑焉。

translations.literal: Though afflicted with loss of speech, Xin was solid in self-conduct, skilled at organizing troops, clear in command and warning, and disciplined in movement; therefore he was trusted and never doubted from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Though mute, he was steady and self-possessed, adept at organizing troops, precise in command and warning, and disciplined in movement—trusted throughout without a shadow of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 有童奴田玉者，能揣度其意，每上前奏事，及與賓客談論，或指揮部下，必回顧玉，書掌為字，玉因直達其意無失。

translations.literal: He had a boy servant Tian Yu who could gauge his intent; whenever he memorialized at court, conversed with guests, or directed subordinates, he would turn to Yu and write characters on his palm; Yu thus conveyed his meaning without fail.
translations.idiomatic: A young servant named Tian Yu could read his mind; whenever Xin appeared at court, entertained guests, or issued orders, he would turn and write on Yu's palm, and Yu never missed his meaning.

sentences.zh: 信未死前一日，瘖疾忽愈，上聞而駭之，遽幸其第。

translations.literal: On the day before Xin's death his speech ailment suddenly cleared; when the emperor heard he was startled and hastened to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The day before he died his voice suddenly returned; the emperor, alarmed, hurried to his house.

sentences.zh: 信自言遭遇兩朝，恩寵隆厚，敘謝感慨，涕泗橫集。

translations.literal: Xin said himself that he had served two reigns with thick favor, spoke thanks with emotion, and tears streamed down.
translations.idiomatic: Xin spoke of serving two reigns with lavish grace, thanked him with feeling, and wept freely.

sentences.zh: 上加慰勉，錫賚有差。

translations.literal: The emperor added comfort and encouragement and bestowed gifts of various grades.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consoled him and sent graded gifts.

sentences.zh: 信弟嗣、贊。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brothers were Si and Zan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers were Si and Zan.

sentences.zh: 弟 嗣

translations.literal: Younger Brother: Si
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother: Si

sentences.zh: 嗣，建隆初以信薦為殿直，三遷崇儀副使、大山軍監軍。

translations.literal: Si, at the beginning of Jianlong through Xin's recommendation became a palace attendant, and after three promotions was vice commissioner of the Ceremonial Guard and military inspector of Dashan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianlong, Si entered service as a palace attendant on his brother's recommendation and rose through three promotions to vice commissioner of the Ceremonial Guard and inspector of the Dashan army.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，就命知軍事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi he was appointed on the spot to command military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4 he was appointed to full command on the spot.

sentences.zh: 代還，以吏民借留再任，俄遷高陽關戰櫂都監。

translations.literal: When his term ended, officials and people begged to keep him for another term; soon he was made director of war boats at Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour ended the locals petitioned to keep him; he was soon made director of war boats at Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，改知保州，門無私謁。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was made prefect of Baozhou; no private callers came to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 2 he was assigned Baozhou and kept his gate free of favor-seekers.

sentences.zh: 轉運使言其治狀，優遷威虜軍，改崇儀使，與曹思進同為靜戎軍、保州、長城、蒲城緣邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner reported on his governance; he was favorably transferred to Weilu army, made Ceremonial Guard commissioner, and with Cao Sijin served together as overall frontier inspector for Jingrong army, Baozhou, Changcheng, and Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner praised his administration; he was promoted into the Weilu command, made Ceremonial Guard commissioner, and with Cao Sijin was named overall frontier inspector for Jingrong, Baozhou, Changcheng, and Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 改如京使，再知保州，有戰功。

translations.literal: He was made envoy to the capital, again governed Baozhou, and had military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Made capital envoy, he governed Baozhou again with combat honors.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加洛苑使。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong took the throne he was given the office of Luoyuan commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenzong's accession he was made Luoyuan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，領獎州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was given Jiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianping he held Jiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，與敵人戰於廉良，斬首二千級，獲戰馬輜重甚眾，以功真拜保州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year he fought the enemy at Lianliang, beheaded two thousand, captured many war horses and baggage, and for merit was truly appointed prefect of Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he fought at Lianliang, took two thousand heads and great spoil, and for that merit received Baozhou in full commission.

sentences.zh: 召還，授本州團練使。

translations.literal: Recalled, he was made regimental commissioner of his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was made regimental commissioner of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時楊延昭方為刺史，嗣言：「嘗與延昭同官，驟居其上，不可，願守舊官。」

translations.literal: When Yang Yanzhao was then prefect, Si said: "I once served with Yanzhao on equal footing; to leap suddenly above him is wrong—I wish to keep my former post."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yanzhao was then prefect of Baozhou; Si said, "We once served as equals—I cannot step above him now and prefer my former rank."

sentences.zh: 上嘉其讓，乃遷延昭官。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his yielding and thereupon promoted Yanzhao's rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his modesty and promoted Yanzhao instead.

sentences.zh: 嗣與延昭久居北邊，俱以善戰聞，時謂之「二楊」。

translations.literal: Si and Yanzhao long dwelt on the northern frontier, both famed for skill in battle, and were called at the time "the Two Yangs."
translations.idiomatic: Having long served on the northern front, both were famed fighters and were known as "the Two Yangs."

sentences.zh: 嗣以武人治郡，不屑細務，又兼領巡徼，在郡日少，城堞圮壞，有未葺者，詔供備庫副使趙彬代之，改深州團練都巡檢使兼保州鈐轄。

translations.literal: Si, as a military man governing a prefecture, disdained petty affairs; he also concurrently held frontier patrol duties and was rarely in the prefecture; ramparts crumbled and some were unrepaired; the emperor ordered Vice Commissioner Zhao Bin of the Supply Depot to replace him, and made Si regimental training overall frontier inspector of Shenzhou concurrently with Baozhou military controller.
translations.idiomatic: A fighter governing a prefecture, Si scorned paperwork and was often away on patrol; walls crumbled unrepaired, so Supply Vice Commissioner Zhao Bin replaced him as prefect while Si became Shenzhou's frontier inspector and Baozhou's military controller.

sentences.zh: 五年，邊人寇保州，嗣與楊延昭禦之，部伍不整，為所襲。

translations.literal: In the fifth year border people raided Baozhou; Si and Yang Yanzhao met them but formations were disorderly and they were attacked.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 raiders struck Baozhou; Si and Yanzhao met them with ranks in disarray and were ambushed.

sentences.zh: 士馬多亡失，代還，特宥其罪。

translations.literal: Many troops and horses were lost; when his term ended he was specially pardoned for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Many men and mounts were lost; on rotation he was specially forgiven.

sentences.zh: 明年，與防秋之策，條陳北面利害，以其練達邊事，出為鎮、定、高陽關三路後陣鈐轄，移定州副都部署，留其家京師，假官第以居。

translations.literal: The next year, participating in autumn-defense planning, he set forth the advantages and harms on the northern front; because he was practiced in border affairs, he was sent out as military controller of the rear echelon for the three circuits Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass, transferred to deputy overall deployer of Dingzhou, his family kept in the capital with an official residence lent for their dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he joined the autumn-defense council, laid out the northern frontier in detail, and—trusted for border expertise—was posted as rear-echelon controller for Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass, made deputy supreme commander at Dingzhou, and left his family in the capital in a lent official mansion.

sentences.zh: 景德初，改鎮州路副都部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was made deputy overall deployer of the Zhenzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingde he was made deputy supreme commander of the Zhenzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 上以嗣耄年總軍政，慮有廢闕，旋命代之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Si was old and oversaw military affairs, feared lapses and soon ordered someone to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, fearing lapses as Si grew old in overall command, soon replaced him.

sentences.zh: 連為趙、貝、深三州部署。

translations.literal: He served in succession as deployer for the three prefectures Zhao, Bei, and Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as deployer for Zhao, Bei, and Shen prefectures.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，復出為天雄軍副都部署。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he was again sent out as deputy overall deployer of the Tianxiong army.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 5 (1012) he was again posted as deputy supreme commander of the Tianxiong army.

sentences.zh: 六年，以左龍武大將軍致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he retired as general of the Left Martial Dragon Corps.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he retired as general of the Left Martial Dragon Corps.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: The next year he died at age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next year at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 錄其子承憲為侍禁。

translations.literal: His son Chengxian was enrolled as a palace attendant guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengxian was enrolled as a palace guard attendant.

sentences.zh: 贊稍知書，無異能，以兄故得掌禁旅，累資朝著至牧守焉。

translations.literal: Zan knew a little of books and had no special talent; because of his elder brother he came to command the palace guard, and through accumulated seniority at court rose to governorships.
translations.idiomatic: Zan had modest learning and no special gifts; through his brother he commanded the palace guard and, by seniority at court, rose to governorships.

sentences.zh: 党進，朔州馬邑人。

translations.literal: Dang Jin was a native of Mayi in Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Jin came from Mayi in Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 幼給事魏帥杜重威，重威愛其淳謹，及壯，猶令與姬妾雜侍。

translations.literal: In youth he served the Wei commander Du Chongwei; Chongwei loved his simple honesty, and even when grown still had him wait among the concubines.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he served the Wei commander Du Chongwei, who prized his plain honesty and, even after he came of age, still kept him waiting among the concubines.

sentences.zh: 重威敗，進以膂力隸軍伍。

translations.literal: When Chongwei was defeated, Jin entered the army ranks on his strength.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongwei's defeat, Jin joined the ranks on his physical strength.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，補散指揮使，累遷鐵騎都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Guangshun he was made an officer of the Scattered Command and was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun reign he entered the Scattered Command and rose to deputy commander of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 宋初，轉本軍都校、領欽州刺史，遷馬步軍副都軍頭、領虔州團練使，改虎捷右廂都指揮使、領睦州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he became colonel of his regiment and prefect of Qinzhou, was promoted to deputy commander-in-chief of the horse and foot armies and regimental commissioner of Qianzhou, and was made commander of the right Tiger Swift column and defense commissioner of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he became regimental colonel and Qinzhou prefect, rose to deputy commander of the horse and foot armies with the Qianzhou regimental commission, and was made commander of the right Tiger Swift column and Muzhou defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，改領閬州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong he was transferred to Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2 he was transferred to Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，改龍捷左廂都虞候、領利州觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he was made deputy commander of the left Dragon Swift column and military commissioner of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande he became deputy commander of the left Dragon Swift column and military commissioner of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 後四年，權步軍。

translations.literal: Four years later he held acting command of the foot army.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he held acting command of the foot army.

sentences.zh: 杜審瓊卒，命進代領其務。

translations.literal: When Du Shenqiong died, Jin was ordered to take over his duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Shenqiong died, Jin was ordered to take over his post.

sentences.zh: 五年，領彰信軍節度兼侍衛步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he held the Zhangxin military commission concurrently with command of the Palace Guard foot army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he held the Zhangxin military commission and command of the Palace Guard foot army.

sentences.zh: 進出戎行，形貌魁岸，居常恂恂，每擐甲胄，毛發皆豎。

translations.literal: Jin came from the military ranks; his physique was towering; in daily life he was modest and respectful, but whenever he donned armor his hair stood on end.
translations.idiomatic: A career soldier of towering build, he was mild in peacetime, yet the moment he buckled on armor his hair bristled.

sentences.zh: 進名進，自稱曰暉，人問之，則曰：「吾欲從吾便耳。」

translations.literal: Jin's given name was Jin; he called himself Hui; when people asked, he said: "I wish to suit my own convenience."
translations.idiomatic: His name was Jin, but he called himself Hui; when asked why, he said, "I want it my own way."

sentences.zh: 先是，禁中軍校，自都虞候已上，悉書所掌兵數於梃上，如笏記焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, palace guard officers from deputy commander upward all wrote the troop numbers they commanded on their batons, like memoranda on court tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guard officers from deputy commander up used to inscribe their troop counts on their batons, like notes on a court tablet.

sentences.zh: 太祖一日問進所掌幾何，進不識字，但舉梃以示於上曰：「盡在是矣。」

translations.literal: One day Taizu asked Jin how many troops he commanded; Jin could not read but only raised his baton to show the emperor, saying: "It is all here."
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizu asked how many men he commanded; illiterate, Jin simply raised his baton and said, "It's all right here."

sentences.zh: 上以其樸直，益厚之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his plain honesty, treated him all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prized his plain honesty and favored him all the more.

sentences.zh: 嘗受詔巡京師，閭里間有畜養禽獸者，見必取而縱之，罵曰：「買肉不將供父母，反以飼禽獸乎。」

translations.literal: Once ordered to patrol the capital, whenever he saw households keeping birds and beasts he would seize and release them, scolding: "You buy meat and do not offer it to your parents, yet feed birds and beasts instead?"
translations.idiomatic: Patrolling the capital on imperial orders, he seized and released every caged bird or beast he found, scolding, "You buy meat for birds instead of your parents?"

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗令親吏臂鷹雛於市，進亟欲放之，吏曰：「此晉王鷹也。」

translations.literal: Taizong once had a personal attendant carry a fledgling hawk through the market; Jin at once wanted to release it; the attendant said: "This is Prince of Jin's hawk."
translations.idiomatic: Once when Taizong had an attendant carry a hawk through the market, Jin moved to release it; the man said, "This is the Prince of Jin's hawk."

sentences.zh: 進乃戒之曰：「汝謹養視。」

translations.literal: Jin then warned him: "You must care for it carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Jin then warned him, "Mind you care for it well."

sentences.zh: 小民傳以為笑，其變詐又如此。

translations.literal: Common folk passed the story around as a joke—his shifty cunning was like this too.
translations.idiomatic: Common folk laughed at the story—his shifty side showed just as plainly.

sentences.zh: 杜重威子孫有貧困者，進分月俸給之，士大夫或有愧焉。

translations.literal: Among Du Chongwei's descendants some were poor; Jin shared his monthly salary with them, and some scholar-officials felt ashamed by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: He shared his monthly salary with impoverished descendants of Du Chongwei, to the shame of some scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 子崇義閑廄使，崇貴閤門祗候。

translations.literal: His sons Chongyi was commissioner of the spare stables, and Chonggui was a gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Chongyi served as spare-stable commissioner and Chonggui as a gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 李漢瓊

translations.literal: Li Hanqiong
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanqiong

sentences.zh: 李漢瓊，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Li Hanqiong was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanqiong came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖裕，祁州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yu was prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yu had been prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 漢瓊體質魁岸，有膂力。

translations.literal: Hanqiong had a towering physique and great strength.
translations.idiomatic: Hanqiong was powerfully built and immensely strong.

sentences.zh: 晉末，補西班衛士，遷內殿直。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin he was made a guard of the Western Shift and was promoted to inner palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jin he joined the Western Shift guard and rose to inner palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，從征淮南，先登，遷龍旗直副都知，改左射指揮使。

translations.literal: During Zhou Xiande he followed the Huainan campaign, was first to scale the walls, was promoted to deputy commander of the Dragon Banner guard, and was made commander of the Left Archers.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiande era he campaigned in Huainan, was first over the wall, rose to deputy commander of the Dragon Banner guard, and became commander of the Left Archers.

sentences.zh: 宋初，再遷鐵騎第二軍都校、領饒州刺史，遷控鶴左廂都校、領瀘州刺史，改澄州團練使，轉虎捷左廂都指揮使、領融州防禦使，遷侍衛馬軍都虞候、領洮州觀察使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was twice promoted to colonel of the second Iron Cavalry regiment and prefect of Raozhou, then colonel of the left Cranes column and prefect of Luzhou, made regimental commissioner of Chengzhou, transferred to commander of the left Tiger Swift column and defense commissioner of Rongzhou, and promoted to deputy commander of the Palace Guard horse army and military commissioner of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he became colonel of the second Iron Cavalry regiment and Raozhou prefect, then colonel of the left Cranes column and Luzhou prefect, regimental commissioner of Chengzhou, commander of the left Tiger Swift column and Rongzhou defense commissioner, and deputy commander of the Palace Guard horse army with the Taozhou military commission.

sentences.zh: 王師征江南，命領行營騎軍兼戰櫂左廂都指揮使，自蘄春攻岐口砦，斬首數千級，獲樓船數百艘，沿流拔池州，破銅陵，取當塗，作浮梁於牛渚以濟大軍。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Jiangnan, he was ordered to lead the field cavalry and commander of the left war-boat column; from Qichun he attacked the Qikou stockade, beheaded several thousand, captured several hundred tower ships, along the river took Chizhou, broke Tongling, seized Dangtu, and built a pontoon bridge at Niuzhu to ferry the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangnan campaign he led the field cavalry and left war-boat column, stormed Qikou stockade from Qichun with thousands of heads taken and hundreds of tower ships captured, seized Chizhou, Tongling, and Dangtu along the river, and threw a pontoon bridge at Niuzhu to ferry the main army.

sentences.zh: 分圍金陵，率所部度秦淮，取巨艦實葦其中，縱火攻其水砦，拔之。

translations.literal: He joined the siege of Jinling, led his troops across the Qinhuai, took great ships stuffed with reeds, set fire to attack their river fort, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Joining the siege of Jinling, he crossed the Qinhuai, packed great ships with reeds, burned the enemy river fort, and took it.

sentences.zh: 江南平，以功領振武軍節度。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, for his merit he was given the Zhenwu military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan fell he received the Zhenwu military commission for his merit.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，出為彰德軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was sent out as military commissioner of the Zhangde army.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 he was posted as military commissioner of Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 四年，太宗親征太原，改攻城都部署。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Taizong personally campaigned against Taiyuan and made him overall deployer of the assault.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Taizong marched on Taiyuan in person and made him supreme commander of the assault.

sentences.zh: 漢瓊與牛思進主攻城南偏，漢瓊先登，矢集其腦，並中指，傷甚猶力疾戰。

translations.literal: Hanqiong and Niu Sijin chiefly attacked the southern flank of the city; Hanqiong was first to ascend; arrows clustered on his head and one struck his middle finger; though gravely wounded he still fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: With Niu Sijin he led the southern assault; first over the wall, he took arrows in the head and a finger, yet fought on despite grave wounds.

sentences.zh: 上召至幄殿，賜良藥以慰勞之。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him to the tent hall and gave fine medicines to comfort and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to the tent hall and gave him fine medicines in reward.

sentences.zh: 先是，攻城者以牛革冒木上，士卒蒙之而進，謂之洞子。

translations.literal: Earlier, assault troops covered timber with oxhide; soldiers sheltered under it as they advanced—this was called a "tunnel shield."
translations.idiomatic: Assault troops had covered timber frames with oxhide for soldiers to advance beneath—called tunnel shields.

sentences.zh: 上欲幸其中，以勞士卒，漢瓊極諫，以為矢石之下，非萬乘之尊所宜輕往，上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to enter one to encourage the troops; Hanqiong strongly remonstrated that under flying arrows and stones it was not fitting for the Son of Heaven lightly to go; the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to enter one to encourage the troops; Hanqiong strongly urged that under flying missiles the Son of Heaven ought not go lightly, and the emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 太原平，改鎮州兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan was pacified, he was made military controller of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiyuan fell he was made military controller of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹數萬騎寇中山，漢瓊與戰於滿城，大敗之，逐至遂城，俘斬萬計，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: Khitan forces in tens of thousands raided Zhongshan; Hanqiong fought them at Mancheng, routed them utterly, pursued to Suicheng, and captured or killed on the order of ten thousand; he was given the honorary title of Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan raiders in the tens of thousands struck Zhongshan, he routed them at Mancheng, pursued to Suicheng, and took ten thousand heads and captives, receiving the honorary title Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸大名，漢瓊上謁，陳邊事稱旨，命為滄州都部署，加賜戰馬、金甲、寶劍、戎具以寵之。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Daming, Hanqiong presented himself; his presentation on frontier affairs pleased the emperor, who appointed him overall deployer of Cangzhou and additionally bestowed war horses, golden armor, a treasured sword, and military gear to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: When the court visited Daming, his frontier briefing pleased the emperor, who named him supreme commander of Cangzhou and added war horses, golden armor, a treasured sword, and kit as marks of favor.

sentences.zh: 六年，以病還京，賜白金萬兩，月餘卒，年五十五，贈中書令。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he returned to the capital on account of illness, was given ten thousand taels of silver, and died a little over a month later at age fifty-five; he was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he returned ill to the capital, received ten thousand taels of silver, and died a month later at fifty-five, posthumously honored as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 漢瓊性木強，使酒難近，然善戰有功。

translations.literal: Hanqiong was stubborn by nature, fond of drink and hard to approach, yet skilled in battle with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Stubborn and hard-drinking, he was not easy company, yet he fought well and earned merit.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟漢贇、漢彬。

translations.literal: He had no sons; his younger brothers were Hanyun and Hanbin.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons; his younger brothers were Hanyun and Hanbin.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，漢贇補供奉官，嘗監高陽關、平戎軍，乘傳衢、婺二州，捕劇賊程白眉數十人，悉殲焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, Hanyun was made a palace attendant, once supervised Gaoyang Pass and Pingrong army, traveled post-haste through Qu and Wu prefectures, and captured several dozen notorious bandits led by Cheng Baimei, destroying them all.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo, Hanyun became a palace attendant, supervised Gaoyang Pass and Pingrong army, rode post through Qu and Wu prefectures, and wiped out dozens of bandits led by Cheng Baimei.

sentences.zh: 累仕崇儀使、知寧州，大中祥符七年卒。

translations.literal: Through accumulated service he became Ceremonial Guard commissioner and prefect of Ningzhou, and died in the seventh year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Ceremonial Guard commissioner and Ningzhou prefect and died in Dazhong Xiangfu 7.

sentences.zh: 漢彬至禮賓副使。

translations.literal: Hanbin rose to vice commissioner of Ceremonial Reception.
translations.idiomatic: Hanbin rose to vice commissioner of Ceremonial Reception.

sentences.zh: 劉遇，滄州清池人。

translations.literal: Liu Yu was a native of Qingchi in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu came from Qingchi in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少魁梧有膂力。

translations.literal: In youth he was tall and powerfully built.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was tall and powerfully built.

sentences.zh: 周祖鎮大名，隸帳下。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder was stationed at Daming, he was attached to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder was posted at Daming, he served on his staff.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，補控鶴都頭，改副指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was made a company head of the Cranes and was changed to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he became a Cranes company head and then deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷御馬直指揮使，俄領漢州刺史，改領眉州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was promoted to commander of the Imperial Horse guard, soon held Hanzhou prefecture, and was transferred to Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he became commander of the Imperial Horse guard, soon held Hanzhou, then Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷控鶴右廂都指揮使、領瓊州團練使。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became commander of the right Cranes column and regimental commissioner of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commander of the right Cranes column and regimental commissioner of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，以功遷虎捷右廂，改領蔚州防禦使。

translations.literal: He followed the Taiyuan campaign and for merit was transferred to the right Tiger Swift column and made defense commissioner of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the Taiyuan campaign he was moved to the right Tiger Swift column and made Weizhou defense commissioner for his merit.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年，轉侍衛步軍都虞候、領洮州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaibao he was made deputy commander of the Palace Guard foot army and military commissioner of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 6 he became deputy commander of the Palace Guard foot army and Taozhou military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 征江南，領步軍戰櫂都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the Jiangnan campaign he commanded the foot army war-boat forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangnan campaign he commanded the foot army war-boat forces.

sentences.zh: 時吳兵三萬屯皖口，遇會諸路兵破之，擒其將朱令贇、王暉等，獲戎器數萬，金陵以平，錄功加領大同軍節度。

translations.literal: At that time Wu forces of thirty thousand were encamped at Wankou; Yu joined troops from all routes to defeat them, captured their generals Zhu Lingyun, Wang Hui, and others, seized tens of thousands of weapons, Jinling was pacified, and his merit was recorded with addition of the Datong military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When thirty thousand Wu troops held Wankou, Yu joined forces from every route, crushed them, captured generals Zhu Lingyun and Wang Hui, seized vast stores of arms, and helped bring Jinling down—earning the Datong military commission.

sentences.zh: 車駕雩祀西洛，命率禁衛以從。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage performed rain-prayer sacrifice in the Western Capital, he was ordered to lead the palace guard in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the court performed rain-prayer rites at Luoyang, he led the palace guard in attendance.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，出為彰信軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo he was sent out as military commissioner of the Zhangxin army.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 he was posted as military commissioner of Zhangxin.

sentences.zh: 四年，征太原，與史珪攻城北面，平之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he campaigned against Taiyuan, with Shi Gui attacked the north face of the city, and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he campaigned against Taiyuan, with Shi Gui took the north face of the city, and brought it down.

sentences.zh: 進攻范陽，師還，坐所部失律，責授宿州觀察使。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Fanyang, when the army returned he was punished because his troops had violated discipline and was demoted to military commissioner of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the advance against Fanyang, when the army withdrew he was punished for disciplinary failures in his command and demoted to Suzhou military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，從幸大名，復保靜軍節度、幽州行營都部署，護築保州、威虜、靜戎、平塞、長城五城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he accompanied the emperor to Daming, was restored to the Baojing military commission and overall deployer of the Youzhou field army, and supervised construction of the five cities Baozhou, Weilu, Jingrong, Pingsai, and Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he accompanied the court to Daming, was restored to the Baojing commission and supreme commander of the Youzhou field army, and oversaw building the five frontier cities Baozhou, Weilu, Jingrong, Pingsai, and Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 八年，徙鎮滑州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to govern Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was transferred to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 晨興方對客，足有灸瘡痛，其醫謂火毒不去，故痛不止。

translations.literal: One morning while receiving guests his foot had pain from a moxibustion sore; his physician said the fire toxin had not departed, and therefore the pain would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: One morning while entertaining guests his foot ached from a moxibustion sore; the physician said lingering fire toxin kept the pain from easing.

sentences.zh: 遇即解衣，取刀割瘡至骨，曰：「火毒去矣。」

translations.literal: Yu at once removed his clothes, took a knife and cut the sore to the bone, saying: "The fire toxin is gone."
translations.idiomatic: Yu stripped, took a knife, and cut the sore to the bone, saying, "The fire toxin is gone."

sentences.zh: 談笑如常時，旬餘乃差。

translations.literal: He conversed and laughed as usual; after ten-odd days he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He chatted and laughed as usual and was healed in little more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 遇性淳謹，待士有禮，尤善射，太宗待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Yu was simple and respectful by nature, treated gentlemen with courtesy, was especially skilled at archery, and Taizong treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and respectful, courteous to gentlemen, and an exceptional archer, he enjoyed Taizong's deep favor.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，卒，年六十六，贈侍中，歸葬京師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he died at age sixty-six, was posthumously made Palace Attendant, and was buried in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongxi 2 at sixty-six, was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant, and was buried in the capital.

sentences.zh: 李懷忠

translations.literal: Li Huaizhong
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaizhong

sentences.zh: 李懷忠，涿州范陽人。

translations.literal: Li Huaizhong was a native of Fanyang in Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaizhong came from Fanyang in Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 初名懷義。

translations.literal: His original name was Huaiyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally named Huaiyi.

sentences.zh: 太祖掌禁兵時，隸帳下為散都頭，累遷殿前都指揮使、都虞候、領開州刺史。

translations.literal: When Taizu commanded the palace guard he was attached to his staff as a scattered company head, and through repeated promotions became commander of the Palace Front, deputy commander, and prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu commanded the palace guard he served on his staff as a company head and rose to commander and deputy commander of the Palace Front and Kaizhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，授東西班都指揮使，改領富州。

translations.literal: During Qiande he was made commander of the Eastern and Western Shift guards and transferred to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande he became commander of the Eastern and Western Shift guards and was transferred to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，從太祖征晉陽，累月未下。

translations.literal: During Kaibao he followed Taizu in campaigning against Jinyang; for many months it was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao he followed Taizu's siege of Jinyang, which dragged on for months.

sentences.zh: 會盛暑，欲班師以休息士卒，懷忠謂：「賊嬰孤城，內無儲偫，外無援兵，其勢危困，若急攻之，破在旦夕，臣願奮銳為士卒先。」

translations.literal: When the heat was intense the emperor wished to withdraw the army to rest the troops; Huaizhong said: "The enemy clings to an isolated city, within there are no stored provisions, without there are no relief troops—their situation is perilous and strained; if we press the attack, capture is within a day or two; your servant wishes to rouse the elite and lead the troops as vanguard."
translations.idiomatic: In the midsummer heat the emperor meant to withdraw and rest the troops; Huaizhong said, "They cling to an isolated city with no stores within and no relief without—press the attack and they fall within days; let me lead the charge."

sentences.zh: 會大熱，戰不利，懷忠中流矢，力疾戰益奮。

translations.literal: In the great heat the battle went badly; Huaizhong was struck by a stray arrow yet fought fiercely despite his wound with growing ardor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fierce heat the assault faltered; struck by an arrow, he fought on all the harder.

sentences.zh: 還授散指揮使，遷富州團練使，改日騎左右廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: On return he was made an officer of the Scattered Command, promoted to regimental commissioner of Fuzhou, and made commander of the left and right Sun-Horse columns.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made an officer of the Scattered Command, regimental commissioner of Fuzhou, and commander of the left and right Sun-Horse columns.

sentences.zh: 上幸西京，愛其地形勢得天下中正，有留都之意。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Western Capital he loved its terrain and position as the empire's center and had thoughts of making it the permanent capital.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Luoyang, the emperor admired its central position and considered making it the permanent capital.

sentences.zh: 懷忠乘間進曰：「東京有汴渠之漕，歲致江、淮米數百萬斛，禁衛數十萬人仰給於此，帑藏重兵皆在焉。

translations.literal: Huaizhong seized an opportunity to advance and said: "The Eastern Capital has transport on the Bian Canal; each year it brings in several million hu of grain from the Yangtze and Huai; several hundred thousand palace guards depend on this for supply; the treasury and main forces are all there.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhong seized a moment to say, "The Eastern Capital feeds on Bian Canal transport—millions of hu from the Yangtze and Huai yearly—and hundreds of thousands of guards and the treasury depend on it.

sentences.zh: 根本安固已久，一旦遽欲遷徙，臣實未見其利。」

translations.literal: The foundation has long been secure and firm; to wish suddenly to move the capital—I truly do not see the advantage."
translations.idiomatic: The foundation has stood firm for ages—I see no gain in moving it now."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the advice and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 米信，舊名海進，本奚族，少勇悍，以善射聞。

translations.literal: Mi Xin, formerly named Haijin, was originally of the Xi people; in youth he was fierce and bold and was known for skill in archery.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Xin, formerly Haijin, was of Xi stock; as a youth he was fierce and famed for archery.

sentences.zh: 周祖即位，隸護聖軍。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder took the throne, he was attached to the Imperial Guard army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder took the throne, he joined the Imperial Guard army.

sentences.zh: 從世宗征高平，以功遷龍捷散都頭。

translations.literal: He followed Shizong in the Gaoping campaign and for merit was promoted to company head of the Dragon Swift scattered command.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizong at Gaoping and rose to company head of the Dragon Swift scattered command for his merit.

sentences.zh: 太祖總禁兵，以信隸麾下，得給使左右，遂委心焉，改名信，署牙校。

translations.literal: When Taizu took overall command of the palace guard he attached Xin under him, obtained service at his side, and thereupon entrusted his heart to him, changed his name to Xin, and appointed him a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took command of the palace guard he kept Xin at his side, won his full trust, renamed him Xin, and made him a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 及即位，補殿前指揮使，遷直長。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Xin was made commander of the Palace Front and promoted to chief attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession Xin became commander of the Palace Front and chief attendant.

sentences.zh: 平揚州日，信執弓矢侍上側，有遊騎將迫乘輿，射之，一發而斃。

translations.literal: On the day Yangzhou was pacified, Xin held bow and arrows attending at the emperor's side; a roaming cavalryman was about to press the imperial carriage; he shot him and with one shot brought him down dead.
translations.idiomatic: When Yangzhou fell, Xin stood bow in hand beside the emperor; a roaming horseman bore down on the carriage—one shot dropped him dead.

sentences.zh: 遷內殿直指揮使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commander of the inner palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the inner palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 開寶元年，改殿前指揮使、領郴州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaibao he was made commander of the Palace Front and prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 1 he became commander of the Palace Front and Chenzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，轉散都頭指揮使，繼領高州團練使。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne he was transferred to commander of the scattered company heads and then held the Gaozhou regimental commission.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he became commander of the scattered company heads and then regimental commissioner of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，遷領洮州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to military commissioner of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 3 he was made Taozhou military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，征太原，命為行營馬步軍指揮使，與田重進分督行營諸軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he campaigned against Taiyuan and was ordered to be commander of the field army horse and foot, sharing supervision of the field armies with Tian Zhongjin.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he campaigned against Taiyuan as commander of the field horse and foot armies, sharing oversight of the field forces with Tian Zhongjin.

sentences.zh: 幷人潛師來犯，信擊敗之，殺其將裴正。

translations.literal: Bing forces came in a stealth column to attack; Xin defeated them and killed their general Pei Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Bing troops struck in a stealth column, Xin routed them and killed their general Pei Zheng.

sentences.zh: 幷州平，遂移兵攻范陽。

translations.literal: When Bingzhou was pacified, he then shifted troops to attack Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Bingzhou fell, he marched on Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 師還，以功擢保順軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, for his merit he was promoted to military commissioner of the Baoshun army.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was made military commissioner of Baoshun for his merit.

sentences.zh: 時信族屬多在塞外，會其兄子全自朔州奮身來歸，召見，俾乘傳詣代州，伺間迎致其親屬，發勁卒護送之。

translations.literal: At that time many of Xin's clansmen were beyond the frontier; his nephew Quan came from Shuozhou at risk of his life to surrender; summoned and received, Xin was ordered to travel post-haste to Daizhou, watch for an opportunity to bring his kin in, and send crack troops to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his kin still lived beyond the frontier; when his nephew Quan risked his life coming from Shuozhou, Xin was sent post-haste to Daizhou to fetch the rest, with crack troops as escort.

sentences.zh: 既而全宿留逾年，邊境斥候嚴，竟不能致。

translations.literal: Before long Quan stayed over a year; frontier scouts were strict, and in the end they could not be brought in.
translations.idiomatic: Quan lingered over a year, frontier watch was tight, and the kin never came.

sentences.zh: 信慷慨歎曰：「吾聞忠孝不兩立，方思以身徇國，安能復顧親戚哉！」

translations.literal: Xin sighed with emotion: "I have heard that loyalty and filial piety cannot both stand—I am now resolved to give my body for the state; how can I again look to kin?"
translations.idiomatic: Xin sighed, "Loyalty and filial piety cannot both stand—I mean to give my life to the state; how can I think of kin now?"

sentences.zh: 北望號慟，戒子侄勿復言。

translations.literal: He looked north and wailed in grief, warning sons and nephews not to speak of it again.
translations.idiomatic: He wailed toward the north and forbade his sons and nephews to raise it again.

sentences.zh: 五年，命與郭守贇等同護定州屯兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was ordered with Guo Shouyun and others jointly to guard the garrison troops at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was ordered with Guo Shouyun and others to guard the Dingzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，遷定州駐泊部署。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year he was made deployer of the Dingzhou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of year 6 he became deployer of the Dingzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 八年，改領彰化軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to military commissioner of the Zhanghua army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was made military commissioner of Zhanghua.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，征幽薊，命信為幽州西北道行營馬步軍都部署，敗契丹於新城。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he campaigned against You and Ji, was ordered to be overall deployer of the northwest Youzhou field army horse and foot, and defeated the Khitan at Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 3 he campaigned in You and Ji as supreme commander of the northwest field horse and foot and routed the Khitan at Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 契丹率眾復來戰，王師稍卻，信獨以麾下龍衛卒三百禦敵，敵圍之數重，矢下如雨，信射中數人，麾下士多死。

translations.literal: The Khitan led their host to fight again; the imperial army drew back somewhat; Xin alone with three hundred Dragon Guard troops under him met the enemy; the enemy surrounded them in several rings; arrows fell like rain; Xin shot several men; many of his troops died.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan returned in force; as the imperial army fell back, Xin alone held them with three hundred Dragon Guards, ringed by enemies and arrows like rain; he killed several but many of his men died.

sentences.zh: 會暮，信持大刀，率從騎大呼，殺數十人，敵遂小卻，信以百餘騎突圍得免。

translations.literal: At dusk Xin took a great blade, led his mounted followers in a great shout, killed several dozen men, the enemy then drew back slightly, and Xin with a little over a hundred horsemen broke the encirclement and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he seized a great blade, led a charge that killed dozens, forced a slight enemy pullback, and broke out with a little over a hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 坐失律，議當死，詔特原之，責授右屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Because of violation of discipline he was judged deserving death; an edict specially pardoned him and demoted him to general of the Right Garrison Guard Corps.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for breach of discipline with death on the books, he was specially pardoned and demoted to general of the Right Garrison Guard Corps.

sentences.zh: 明年，復授彰武軍節度。

translations.literal: The next year he was again given the Zhangwu military commission.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he received the Zhangwu military commission again.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，詔置方田，以信為邢州兵馬都部署以監之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong an edict established equal-field land; Xin was made overall deployer of Xingzhou horse and foot to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duangong, when equal-field land was ordered, Xin was made supreme commander of Xingzhou forces to oversee it.

sentences.zh: 二年，改鎮橫海軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to govern the Henghai army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was transferred to the Henghai command.

sentences.zh: 信不知書，所為多暴橫，上命何承矩為之副，以決州事。

translations.literal: Xin could not read; his conduct was mostly violent and overbearing; the emperor ordered He Chengju as his deputy to decide prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Illiterate and brutal in office, he was given He Chengju as deputy to decide state affairs.

sentences.zh: 及承矩領護屯田，信遂專恣不法，軍人宴犒甚薄，嘗私市絹附上計吏，稱官物以免關征，上廉知之。

translations.literal: When Chengju took charge of garrison farming, Xin then acted willfully and unlawfully on his own; rewards for troops at banquets were very thin; he once privately bought silk and sent it to the reporting clerk, calling it official goods to avoid transit duties—the emperor learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengju took over garrison farming, Xin ruled lawlessly, stinted troop rewards, smuggled silk as official goods to evade duties—and the emperor learned of it.

sentences.zh: 四年，召為右武衛上將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned as senior general of the Right Martial Guard Corps.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was recalled as senior general of the Right Martial Guard Corps.

sentences.zh: 明年，判左右金吾街仗事。

translations.literal: The next year he was made superintendent of the left and right Golden Crow street guards.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he superintended the left and right Golden Crow street guards.

sentences.zh: 未逾月，吏卒以無罪被捶撻者甚眾。

translations.literal: Within less than a month very many clerks and soldiers were flogged though guilty of no crime.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he had flogged countless innocent clerks and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 強市人物，妻死買地營葬，妄發居民塚墓。

translations.literal: He forced purchases from people; when his wife died he bought land for burial and wantonly opened residents' tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He extorted goods from the market, bought land for his wife's burial by opening commoners' graves, and seized plots by force.

sentences.zh: 家奴陳贊老病，箠之致死，為其家人所告。

translations.literal: His household slave Chen Zan was old and ill; he beat him to death and was denounced by Zan's family.
translations.idiomatic: He beat his aged, ill slave Chen Zan to death, and the family brought charges.

sentences.zh: 下御史鞫之，信具伏。

translations.literal: The case was sent down to the censorate for trial; Xin confessed in full.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate tried him and Xin confessed fully.

sentences.zh: 獄未上而卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: Before the case was submitted he died at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-seven before the case reached court.

sentences.zh: 贈橫海軍節度。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the Henghai military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the Henghai military commission.

sentences.zh: 子繼豐，內殿崇班、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: His son Jifeng was of the inner palace honored company and a gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jifeng served in the inner palace honored company and as a gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 田重進

translations.literal: Tian Zhongjin
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhongjin

sentences.zh: 田重進，幽州人。

translations.literal: Tian Zhongjin was a native of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhongjin came from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 形質奇偉，有武力。

translations.literal: His physique was singular and imposing, and he had martial strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was imposing in build and possessed great martial strength.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，應募為卒，隸太祖麾下。

translations.literal: During Zhou Xiande he enlisted as a soldier and was attached to Taizu's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiande era he enlisted and served under Taizu.

sentences.zh: 從征契丹，至陳橋還，遷御馬軍使，積功至瀼州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the Khitan, returned at Chenqiao, was promoted to commander of the Imperial Horse army, and through accumulated merit reached prefect of Rangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the Khitan, returned at Chenqiao, rose to commander of the Imperial Horse army, and through merit became Rangzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，從征太原還，錄功擢為天德軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo he returned from the Taiyuan campaign and, his merit recorded, was promoted to military commissioner of the Tiande army.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4 he returned from Taiyuan and was made military commissioner of Tiande for his recorded merit.

sentences.zh: 六年，改侍衛步軍指揮使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made commander of the Palace Guard foot army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he became commander of the Palace Guard foot army.

sentences.zh: 八年，改領靜難軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to military commissioner of the Jingnan army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was made military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 九年，河決滑州韓房村，重進總護其役，以劉吉為之副，河遂塞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Yellow River broke its banks at Hanfang village in Huazhou; Zhongjin oversaw the works in chief, with Liu Ji as deputy, and the river was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 the Yellow River burst at Hanfang in Huazhou; Zhongjin oversaw the repair with Liu Ji as deputy, and the breach was sealed.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，出師北征，重進率兵傅飛狐城下，用袁繼忠計，伏兵飛狐南口，擒契丹驍將大鵬翼及其監軍馬贇、副將何萬通並渤海軍三千餘人，斬首數千級，俘獲以萬計，逐北四十里，連下飛狐、靈州等城。

translations.literal: During Yongxi the army marched north; Zhongjin led troops to the foot of Feihu city, used Yuan Jizhong's plan to set ambush at the southern pass of Feihu, captured the Khitan fierce general Dapengyi and his supervising commander Ma Yun, deputy He Wantong, and more than three thousand Bohai troops, beheaded several thousand, captives and booty in the tens of thousands, pursued north forty li, and in succession took Feihu, Lingzhou, and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the northern campaign of Yongxi he besieged Feihu, ambushed the southern pass on Yuan Jizhong's plan, captured the Khitan general Dapengyi with Ma Yun and He Wantong and over three thousand Bohai troops, took thousands of heads and tens of thousands of captives, pursued forty li, and seized Feihu, Lingzhou, and other cities in turn.

sentences.zh: 進攻蔚州，其牙校李存璋等殺酋帥蕭啜理、執耿紹忠，率吏民來附。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Weizhou, its staff officer Li Cunzhang and others killed the chieftain Xiao Chuoli, seized Geng Shaozhong, and led officials and people to submit.
translations.idiomatic: At Weizhou his staff officer Li Cunzhang killed the chieftain Xiao Chuoli, seized Geng Shaozhong, and brought officials and people over.

sentences.zh: 會曹彬之師不利，乃命重進董師駐定州，遷定州駐泊兵馬都部署。

translations.literal: When Cao Bin's army fared badly, Zhongjin was ordered to take charge of the army stationed at Dingzhou and was made overall deployer of the Dingzhou garrison horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Bin's force faltered, he was put in charge at Dingzhou and made supreme commander of the garrison there.

sentences.zh: 三年，率師入遼境，攻下岐溝關，殺守城兵千餘及獲牛馬輜重以還。

translations.literal: In the third year he led troops into Liao territory, took Qigou Pass, killed more than a thousand garrison troops, and returned with cattle, horses, and baggage.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he invaded Liao territory, took Qigou Pass, killed over a thousand defenders, and returned with cattle, horses, and baggage.

sentences.zh: 四年春，改彰信軍節度。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he was transferred to the Zhangxin military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 4 he was transferred to the Zhangxin military commission.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，改真定尹、成德軍節度。
