translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he was made metropolitan prefect of Zhending and military commissioner of the Chengde army.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 3 he became metropolitan prefect of Zhending and military commissioner of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移京兆尹、永興軍節度。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and military commissioner of the Yongxing army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was moved to metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and military commissioner of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 五年，改知延州，復還鎮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made prefect of Yanzhou and then returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was assigned Yanzhou, then returned to his former command.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，卒，年六十九，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao he died at age sixty-nine and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhidao 3 at sixty-nine and was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 重進不事學，太宗居藩邸時，愛其忠勇，嘗遺以酒炙不受，使者曰：「此晉王賜也，何為不受？」

translations.literal: Zhongjin did not pursue learning; when Taizong was in the princely residence he loved his loyalty and courage, once sent him wine and roast meat which he would not accept; the messenger said: "This is the Prince of Jin's gift—why not accept?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjin had no schooling; when Taizong was still in his princely residence he prized his loyalty and once sent wine and meat, which Zhongjin refused; the messenger said, "This is the Prince of Jin's gift—why refuse?"

sentences.zh: 重進曰：「為我謝晉王，我知有天子爾。」

translations.literal: Zhongjin said: "Thank the Prince of Jin for me—I know only the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjin said, "Thank the Prince of Jin for me—I know only the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 卒不受。

translations.literal: In the end he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He still would not accept.

sentences.zh: 上知其忠樸，故終始委遇焉。

translations.literal: The emperor knew his loyal simplicity and therefore entrusted and favored him from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew his loyal plainness and favored him throughout.

sentences.zh: 子守信六宅使，守吉閤門祗候。

translations.literal: His sons Shouxin was commissioner of the Six Residences, and Shouji was a gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shouxin served as commissioner of the Six Residences and Shouji as a gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 劉廷翰

translations.literal: Liu Tinghan
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tinghan

sentences.zh: 太宗北伐，既班師，上以邊備在於得人，乃命廷翰、李漢瓊率兵屯真定，崔彥進屯關南，崔翰屯定州。

translations.literal: After Taizong's northern campaign and withdrawal, the emperor held that frontier defense lay in getting the right men; he ordered Tinghan and Li Hanqiong to lead troops stationed at Zhending, Cui Yanjin at Guannan, and Cui Han at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's northern campaign withdrew, he posted Tinghan and Li Hanqiong at Zhending, Cui Yanjin south of the passes, and Cui Han at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，契丹果縱兵南侵。

translations.literal: In winter the Khitan indeed loosed troops to invade south.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Khitan duly invaded south.

sentences.zh: 廷翰先陣於徐河，彥進率師出黑蘆堤北，銜枚躡契丹後，崔翰、漢瓊兵繼至，合擊之，大敗其眾於滿城。

translations.literal: Tinghan first formed battle lines at the Xu River; Yanjin led troops out north of Heilu Embankment, took gags and followed the Khitan rear; Cui Han's and Hanqiong's forces came up after, joined in the attack, and routed their host at Mancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tinghan drew up at the Xu River; Yanjin slipped behind the Khitan north of Heilu Embankment with gagged men; Cui Han and Hanqiong came up, and together they routed the enemy at Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 廷翰以功領大同軍節度、殿前都虞候。

translations.literal: For his merit Tinghan was given the Datong military commission and made deputy commander of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he received the Datong military commission and became deputy commander of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 八年，改領彰信軍節度。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to the Zhangxin military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was transferred to the Zhangxin military commission.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年春，改鎮滑、邢。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year of Yongxi he was transferred to govern Hua and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Yongxi 4 he was transferred to Hua and Xing prefectures.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，鎮州駐泊馬步軍都部署郭守文卒，上特命廷翰代之。

translations.literal: During Duangong, Guo Shouwen, overall deployer of the Zhenzhou garrison horse and foot, died; the emperor specially ordered Tinghan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: During Duangong, when Guo Shouwen, supreme commander of the Zhenzhou garrison, died, the emperor named Tinghan to replace him.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，改大名尹、天雄軍節度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he was made metropolitan prefect of Daming and military commissioner of the Tianxiong army.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 3 he became metropolitan prefect of Daming and military commissioner of Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 三年，以病求解官，還闕，上親臨問，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: In the third year, on account of illness he requested release from office, returned to court, and the emperor personally visited to inquire and gave additional gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he asked to resign, returned to court, and the emperor visited him in person with added gifts.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年七十，贈侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he died at age seventy and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after at seventy and was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 廷翰自衛士至上將，頗以武勇自任，寬厚容眾，雖不事威嚴，而長於御下。

translations.literal: From guard soldier to senior general, Tinghan rather prided himself on martial courage, was generous and tolerant of the multitude, and though he did not affect stern majesty, he was skilled at commanding subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from guard to senior general, he prided himself on martial courage, was generous with his men, and though not stern in manner excelled at command.

sentences.zh: 為殿前都指揮使，入朝，常行眾中，每歷宮殿門，少識之者。

translations.literal: As commander of the Palace Front, when he entered court he commonly walked among the crowd; each time he passed palace gates few recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: As commander of the Palace Front he often walked unnoticed among the crowd at court, and few at the palace gates knew him.

sentences.zh: 嘗與郊祀恩，當追封三世，廷翰少孤，其大父以上皆不逮事，忘其家諱，上為撰名親書賜之。

translations.literal: Once, sharing in suburban-sacrifice grace, he was to receive posthumous enfeoffment for three generations; Tinghan was orphaned young; his great-grandfather and above had all died before he could serve them, and he forgot his family taboo names—the emperor composed the names and personally wrote them as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: When suburban-sacrifice grace called for enfeoffing three generations, the orphaned Tinghan had forgotten his ancestors' taboo names; the emperor composed them and wrote them out himself.

sentences.zh: 子贊元，宮苑使、澄州刺史；

translations.literal: His son Zanyuan was palace-garden commissioner and prefect of Chengzhou;
translations.idiomatic: His son Zanyuan was palace-garden commissioner and Chengzhou prefect;

sentences.zh: 贊明，皇城使、勤州團練使。

translations.literal: Zanming was metropolitan guard commissioner and regimental commissioner of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zanming was metropolitan guard commissioner and regimental commissioner of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 崔翰，字仲文，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Cui Han, style name Zhongwen, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Han, style name Zhongwen, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少有大志，風姿偉秀，太祖見而奇之，以隸麾下。

translations.literal: In youth he had great ambition; his bearing was imposing and handsome; Taizu saw him and found him remarkable, and placed him under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious in youth and imposing in bearing, he caught Taizu's eye and entered his service.

sentences.zh: 從周世宗征淮南，平壽春，取關南，以功補軍使。

translations.literal: He followed Zhou Shizong in the Huainan campaign, pacified Shouchun, took Guannan, and for merit was made an army officer.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shizong in Huainan, took Shouchun and Guannan, and became an army officer for his merit.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷御馬直副指揮使，從征澤、潞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was promoted to deputy commander of the Imperial Horse guard and followed the campaigns in Ze and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he became deputy commander of the Imperial Horse guard and campaigned in Ze and Lu.

sentences.zh: 開寶初，遷河東降民以實陝西地，晉人勇悍，多習武藝，命翰差擇之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaibao surrendered people of Hedong were moved to populate Shaanxi; Jin people were fierce and bold and many practiced martial arts—Han was ordered to select among them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaibao, when Hedong surrenderers were settled in Shaanxi, the fierce Jin people—many trained in arms—were put under Han's selection.

sentences.zh: 及閱試河北鎮兵，取其驍果者以分配天武兩軍。

translations.literal: When he reviewed and tested the Hebei garrison troops, he took the boldest and assigned them to the two Heavenly Martial armies.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing Hebei garrison troops, he drafted the boldest into the two Heavenly Martial armies.

sentences.zh: 九年，領端州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he held Duanzhou prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he held Duanzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，從征太原，命總侍衛馬步諸軍，率先攻城，流矢中其頰，神色不變，督戰益急，上即軍帳撫問之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the Taiyuan campaign, was ordered to command all Palace Guard horse and foot, was first to assault the city, was struck in the cheek by a stray arrow yet his expression did not change and he pressed the battle all the more urgently; the emperor came to the army tent to comfort and inquire of him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 at Taiyuan he commanded all Palace Guard horse and foot, led the assault, took an arrow in the cheek without flinching, and pressed the fight harder—the emperor came to the tent to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 太原平，時上將有事幽薊，諸將以為晉陽之役，師罷餉匱，劉繼元降，賞賚且未給，遽有平燕之議，不敢言。

translations.literal: When Taiyuan was pacified the emperor was about to act in You and Ji; the generals thought that after the Jinyang campaign the army was weary and supplies exhausted, Liu Jiyuan had just surrendered, rewards were not yet distributed, and to rush into talk of pacifying Yan was something they dared not voice.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiyuan fell the emperor meant to move on You and Ji, but the generals, mindful of exhausted troops, empty stores, fresh surrender, and unpaid rewards, dared not speak against a Yan campaign.

sentences.zh: 翰獨奏曰：「所當乘者勢也。

translations.literal: Han alone memorialized: "What one should ride is momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Han alone memorialized, "What we must ride is momentum.

sentences.zh: 不可失者時也，取之易。」

translations.literal: What cannot be lost is timing—the taking is easy."
translations.idiomatic: What we cannot lose is timing—the taking will be easy."

sentences.zh: 上謂然，定議北伐。

translations.literal: The emperor said he was right and fixed the decision for a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and fixed on a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 既而班師，命諸將整暇以還。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew he ordered the generals to return at an orderly pace.
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawal he ordered the generals to return in good order.

sentences.zh: 至金臺驛，大軍南向而潰，上令翰率衛兵千餘止之。

translations.literal: At Jintai Post the great army broke southward in rout; the emperor ordered Han to lead more than a thousand guard troops to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: At Jintai Post the army broke south in rout; the emperor sent Han with a thousand guards to halt it.

sentences.zh: 翰請單騎往，至則諭以師律，眾徐以定，不戮一人。

translations.literal: Han asked to go alone on horseback; when he arrived he instructed them in military discipline, the host slowly settled, and not one man was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He rode in alone, restored discipline by word alone, and calmed the host without executing a man.

sentences.zh: 既復命，上喜，因命知定州，得以便宜從事，緣邊諸軍並受節制，軍市租儲，得以專用。

translations.literal: On reporting back the emperor was pleased and thereupon appointed him prefect of Dingzhou with discretionary authority, all frontier armies under his command, and exclusive use of garrison market taxes and stores.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting back, he pleased the emperor, who made him Dingzhou prefect with full discretion, command of all frontier armies, and sole use of garrison revenues.

sentences.zh: 冬，契丹兵數萬寇蒲城，翰會李漢瓊兵於徐河，河陽節度崔彥進兵自高陽關繼至，因合擊之。

translations.literal: In winter Khitan forces in the tens of thousands raided Pucheng; Han joined Li Hanqiong's troops at the Xu River; Heyang commissioner Cui Yanjin's force came up from Gaoyang Pass, and they joined in the attack.
translations.idiomatic: That winter tens of thousands of Khitan raided Pucheng; Han joined Hanqiong at the Xu River, Yanjin came from Gaoyang Pass, and together they struck.

sentences.zh: 契丹投西山坑谷中死者不可勝計，俘馘數萬，所獲他物又十倍焉。

translations.literal: Khitan who threw themselves into western hills and ravines died beyond counting; captives and heads numbered in the tens of thousands, and other goods taken were tenfold again.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan dead in the western hills were beyond count; captives and heads ran to the tens of thousands, with ten times as much other spoil.

sentences.zh: 以功擢武泰軍節度使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to military commissioner of the Wutai army.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made military commissioner of Wutai.

sentences.zh: 初，劉繼元降，上令翰往撫慰，俘略無得出城。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Jiyuan surrendered, the emperor ordered Han to go comfort the people; captives and plunder were not permitted to leave the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jiyuan surrendered, Han was sent to reassure the people and forbid captives or loot to leave the city.

sentences.zh: 時秦王廷美以數十騎將冒禁出，翰嗬止之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Qin Tingmei with several dozen horsemen was about to break the prohibition and go out; Han shouted and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qin Tingmei tried to ride out with several dozen men in defiance of the ban, Han shouted him down.

sentences.zh: 至是，構於上。

translations.literal: By then he had slandered Han to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had slandered Han to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，出為感德軍節度使。

translations.literal: The next summer he was sent out as military commissioner of the Gande army.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer he was posted as military commissioner of Gande.

sentences.zh: 至鎮時，盜賊充斥，翰誘其渠魁，戒以禍福，群盜感悟，散歸農畝，境內肅然。

translations.literal: On reaching his command bandits were everywhere; Han enticed their chiefs, warned them of fortune and calamity, the bandits were moved to understanding, dispersed back to farming, and the territory became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he persuaded bandit chiefs with warnings of fortune and ruin; they dispersed to the fields, and the territory grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，移知滑州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was moved to govern Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 2 he was assigned Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，北伐不利，上追念徐河之功，召翰為威虜軍行營兵馬都部署。

translations.literal: In the third year the northern campaign went badly; the emperor recalled Han's merit at the Xu River and summoned him as overall deployer of the Weilu field army horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, when the northern campaign faltered, the emperor recalled his Xu River victory and named him supreme commander of the Weilu field army.

sentences.zh: 四年春，改鎮定國軍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he was transferred to the Dingguo army.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 4 he was transferred to the Dingguo command.

sentences.zh: 二年，移鎮鎮安軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to the Zhen'an army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was transferred to the Zhen'an command.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年召還，以疾留京師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he was recalled and remained in the capital on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled in Chunhua 3, he stayed in the capital on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 稍間，入見上曰：「臣既以身許國，不願死於家，得以馬革裹屍足矣。」

translations.literal: When somewhat recovered he entered to see the emperor and said: "Your servant has already pledged body to the state; I do not wish to die at home—to have my corpse wrapped in horse hide is enough."
translations.idiomatic: When somewhat recovered he told the emperor, "I have pledged my body to the state—I do not wish to die at home; horsehide for a shroud is enough."

sentences.zh: 上壯之，復令赴鎮，月餘卒，年六十三，贈侍中。

translations.literal: The emperor was impressed, again ordered him to his command, and a little over a month later he died at age sixty-three, posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved, sent him back to his post, and he died a month later at sixty-three, posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 翰驍勇有謀，所至多立功。

translations.literal: Han was fierce and brave with stratagems; wherever he went he often achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce, brave, and resourceful, he won merit wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 輕財好施，死之日家無餘貲。

translations.literal: He treated wealth lightly and loved to give; on the day he died his household had no surplus property.
translations.idiomatic: Generous with wealth, he left nothing in his house when he died.

sentences.zh: 晚年酷信釋氏。

translations.literal: In his later years he ardently believed in Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he became ardently devoted to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 子繼顒，虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Jiyong was an outer vice director of the Parks Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiyong was an outer vice director of the Parks Bureau.

sentences.zh: 孫承業，內殿承制、閣閤門祗候；

translations.literal: His grandson Chengye was an inner palace commissioner and gate attendant of the Pavilion Gate;
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Chengye was an inner palace commissioner and Pavilion Gate attendant;

sentences.zh: 承佑，內殿崇班。

translations.literal: Chengyou was of the inner palace honored company.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyou served in the inner palace honored company.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自曹翰而下，嘗任將帥居節鎮者凡十人，其初率由拳勇起家戎行，雖不事問學，而皆精白一心，以立事功。

translations.literal: The discussion says: From Cao Han downward, those who once served as generals holding military commissions numbered ten in all; at first they mostly rose from the army ranks through boxing courage, and though they did not pursue learning, all were pure in heart and single-minded in establishing achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: From Cao Han down, ten men in this chapter once held frontier commands. Most rose through raw courage in the ranks; though unlearned, each gave himself wholly to merit.

sentences.zh: 始終匹休，而無韓、彭之禍者，由制御保全之有道也。

translations.literal: They were matched in standing from beginning to end and suffered none of the calamity of Han Xin and Peng Yue—this was because control and preservation were conducted with proper method.
translations.idiomatic: They kept their standing to the end and escaped the fate of Han Xin and Peng Yue because the dynasty knew how to control and preserve its commanders.

sentences.zh: 楊信以篤實，重進以忠樸，劉遇以淳謹，廷翰以武勇稱，故皆終始委遇而不替。

translations.literal: Yang Xin was noted for solid sincerity, Zhongjin for loyal simplicity, Liu Yu for plain respectfulness, and Tinghan for martial courage; therefore all were entrusted from beginning to end without change.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xin was valued for steadfast sincerity, Tian Zhongjin for loyal plainness, Liu Yu for respectful decorum, and Liu Tinghan for martial courage—each trusted without fail from first to last.

sentences.zh: 漢瓊雖木強使酒，米信所為雖多暴橫，党進恂恂類懷姦詐，懷忠論遷似昧大體；

translations.literal: Li Hanqiong, though stubborn and fond of drink; Mi Xin, though his conduct was mostly violent and overbearing; Dang Jin, respectful in manner yet seeming to harbor crafty deceit; Li Huaizhong, whose memorial on moving the capital seemed blind to the larger pattern—
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanqiong was stubborn and hard-drinking; Mi Xin often brutal; Dang Jin looked humble yet seemed crafty; Li Huaizhong's argument against moving the capital seemed to miss the larger pattern—

sentences.zh: 然以征太原、平江南、戰徐河觀之，皆不害其為驍果也。

translations.literal: yet judging by the campaigns at Taiyuan, the pacification of Jiangnan, and the battle at the Xu River, none of this detracted from their being fierce and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: yet judged by Taiyuan, Jiangnan, and the Xu River, none of that kept them from being fierce fighters.

sentences.zh: 至於好謀善戰，輕財好施，所至立功，則未有優於曹翰、崔翰者也。

translations.literal: As for skill in stratagem and battle, treating wealth lightly and loving to give, and achieving merit wherever they went, none surpassed Cao Han and Cui Han.
translations.idiomatic: In strategy, combat, generosity, and merit won wherever they served, none outdid Cao Han and Cui Han.

sentences.zh: 然不可與古之良將同日而語者，崔之論奏平燕，未免出於率爾；

translations.literal: Yet they cannot be spoken of in the same day as the fine generals of antiquity: Cui's memorial urging pacification of Yan could not avoid being somewhat rash;
translations.idiomatic: Yet they cannot rank with the great generals of old: Cui's memorial urging a Yan campaign was somewhat rash;

sentences.zh: 而曹之殺降卒，屠江州，則又過於忍者也。

translations.literal: and Cao's killing surrendered troops and slaughter at Jiangzhou were again excessive in ruthlessness.
translations.idiomatic: and Cao's killing of surrendered troops and the Jiangzhou massacre were excessively cruel.

sentences.zh: 君子謂功莫優於二子，而過亦莫先於二子，信矣。

translations.literal: The noble-minded say that in merit none surpassed these two, and in fault none preceded them either—this is truly so.
translations.idiomatic: The noble-minded are right: in merit none surpassed those two, and in fault none led them either.
